answer: Project sensors are declared in the project's settings, and orbit runs them only after the user approves that exact set of commands on this machine; any change to them needs approval again.
effect: Until the user approves the current set on a machine, orbit runs none of them there and records each as unable to read, which counts as firing; a cloned project runs nothing until its user approves, and an AI editing a sensor trips the wire instead of silencing it. Orbit records when each approval was given, so an approval given while a change is under way is noted.

defines.definition: A check orbit runs over the code, the change and its history that reports whether a run has gone off course.
A sensor a project adds itself, by naming a command (such as a linter) whose output orbit reads.
